summary: Commented-out debug sync/modified blocks ('// added debug', '// debug') remain in VerletKokkos::run() at lines 350-352, 359-361, 371-373 and 379-381.
evidence: verlet_kokkos.cpp:350-352 '// added debug / //atomKK->sync(Host,ALL_MASK); / //atomKK->modified(Host,ALL_MASK);' and three more identical blocks. Project review rules: commented-out code added for debugging purposes should be removed entirely.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; release-hygiene item flagged by the project's own review checklist.
suggested_fix: Delete the four commented-out debug blocks.

summary: build_topology() syncs the device-built bond/angle/dihedral/improper lists to the host only when the corresponding force style has execution_space == Host, but other host-side consumers read neighbor->bondlist through the plain pointer (fix bond/break, compute stress/cartesian, pair mesocnt, the library's neigh_bondlist export) and so see a never-updated host copy.
evidence: neighbor_kokkos.cpp:435-442: 'if (force->bond && force->bond->execution_space == Host) k_bondlist.sync_host();' (same for angle/dihedral/improper). neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp:288 grow_kokkos(k_bondlist,neighbor->bondlist,...) points the plain pointer at the host view; :305 'k_bondlist.modify<DeviceType>()' after the device build, and nothing else syncs it. Host readers with no KOKKOS variant (none of these exist in src/KOKKOS): src/MC/fix_bond_break.cpp:239-245 'int **bondlist = neighbor->bondlist; ... i1 = bondlist[n][0]; i2 = bondlist[n][1]; type = bondlist[n][2];', src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_stress_cartesian.cpp:374-378, src/library.cpp:2345 'return (void *) lmp->neighbor->bondlist' (lammps_extract_global "neigh_bondlist"). neighbor->nbondlist (the count) IS correct on the host (neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp:284), so these loops run over nbondlist rows of stale/zero host data.
failure_scenario: GPU run with bond_style harmonic/kk (device list) plus 'fix bond/break' on a polymer: the fix iterates nbondlist rows whose host contents are zero-initialized (never synced), 'type != btype' skips every row, so no bond is ever broken and no error is raised. A Python/library driver reading neigh_bondlist gets the same stale data. On CPU-only Kokkos builds host and device views alias, so the problem only appears on GPU.
suggested_fix: Sync the topology lists to the host whenever any non-KOKKOS style may read them (simplest: sync when force->bond exists and either execution_space == Host or any fix/compute in modify is not kokkosable), or provide a Neighbor::get_bondlist-style accessor that syncs on demand and route the host consumers through it.

summary: In non-GPU-aware mode remap_3d_kokkos() re-creates the host mirrors of the scratch and send buffers with Kokkos::create_mirror_view() on every call, i.e. a fresh host allocation of the full scratch size for each of the several remaps per FFT per timestep.
evidence: remap_kokkos.cpp:123-128: 'if (!plan->usegpu_aware) { plan->h_scratch = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(d_scratch); plan->h_sendbuf = Kokkos::create_mirror_view(plan->d_sendbuf); ... }' executed unconditionally at the top of every remap_3d_kokkos() call; on a GPU backend create_mirror_view allocates (d_scratch is not host accessible). The plan struct keeps h_scratch/h_sendbuf as members, so they could be allocated once (or resized when the extents change).
failure_scenario: PPPM/kk on a GPU without GPU-aware MPI: each timestep performs 4 remaps per 3d FFT (2-3 FFTs), each allocating and freeing a host buffer of nqty*out.isize*out.jsize*out.ksize FFT_SCALARs; pure overhead, no wrong results.
suggested_fix: Allocate h_scratch/h_sendbuf once in remap_3d_create_plan_kokkos (or lazily when their extent differs from the device view), not on every call.

summary: The extent check in the TransposeHelperKokkos constructor compares the destination's second extent with itself instead of with the source, so a mismatched extent(1) is never caught.
evidence: transpose_helper_kokkos.h:78: 'assert(d_dst.extent(0) == d_src.extent(0) && d_dst.extent(1) == d_dst.extent(1));' -- the second operand is trivially true; intended is 'd_dst.extent(1) == d_src.extent(1)'.
failure_scenario: A caller passing views whose second extents differ (e.g. after a maxneighs change on only one of them) is not caught in debug builds; the transpose then reads or writes out of bounds instead of asserting. No effect on release builds (assert compiled out).
suggested_fix: Change the second comparison to d_src.extent(1).

summary: ThirdOrderKokkos::update_force() treats only styles with execution_space == Host as host styles, whereas VerletKokkos::host_force_styles() also treats HostKK (the kk/host variants); a kk/host pair style combined with a device bonded style therefore never gets its forces merged into the device force array.
evidence: third_order_kokkos.cpp:172-207 test 'force->pair->execution_space==Host' (and the same for bond/angle/dihedral/improper/kspace); verlet_kokkos.cpp:697-702 uses '(style->execution_space != HostKK) && (style->execution_space != Host)' to decide. With a HostKK pair style: modified(HostKK,F_MASK) at line 222, then a device bond style does modified(Device,F_MASK) at 243; the DualView's later sync(Host,F_MASK) at 308 copies device -> host and discards the pair forces (no merge, since execute_on_host is false). dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp has the same structure (not in this group).
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'pair_style lj/cut/kk/host' + 'bond_style harmonic/kk' + 'third_order ...': the third-order force constants miss the pair contribution. Unusual combination; the plain Host and plain Device cases are handled.
suggested_fix: Use the same HostKK-or-Host predicate (or reuse VerletKokkos::host_force_styles logic) in ThirdOrderKokkos and DynamicalMatrixKokkos.

summary: TuneKokkos opens its log file only on rank 0 and calls the collective error->all() inside that rank-0-only branch, so a failure to open the file makes rank 0 abort collectively while every other rank continues, i.e. a hang or an MPI abort mismatch in parallel runs; the file is also handled with raw fopen/fclose instead of SafeFilePtr.
evidence: tune_kokkos.cpp:96-104: 'if (comm->me == 0) { std::string filename = fmt::format("tuning-{}.log", my_name); tuning_logfile = fopen(filename.c_str(),"w"); if (tuning_logfile == nullptr) error->all(FLERR,"Cannot open tuning logfile {}: {}", ...); } else { tuning_logfile = nullptr; }'. Project rules: error->all() only when all ranks hit the error, error->one() for a single rank; prefer SafeFilePtr for FILE* resources.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank KOKKOS run with 'package kokkos ... tune' in a read-only working directory: rank 0 enters Error::all (MPI_Barrier/abort protocol), the other ranks proceed to allocate() and into the run -> deadlock or an unclean abort instead of the intended error message.
suggested_fix: Use error->one() for the rank-0 failure (or broadcast the failure flag and call error->all on every rank), and hold the FILE* in a SafeFilePtr.

summary: get_optimal_combination_idx() seeds opt_perf with the raw sample performance[0][0] instead of the representative value of combination 0, so in AVERAGE/MEDIAN mode opt_perf can be a single outlier sample that no combination's representative value beats; the returned index is then 0 with an inflated opt_perf, and regular_performance_check() later measures every real performance against it and can trigger spurious re-scans.
evidence: tune_kokkos.cpp:465-466 'opt_perf = performance[0][0]; int opt_idx = 0;' followed by the loop computing p_i (max/average/median per combination) and 'if (p_i > opt_perf) { opt_perf = p_i; opt_idx = i; }' (496-499). With mode AVERAGE_VALUE or MEDIAN_VALUE, p_0 <= max sample of row 0, so a large performance[0][0] is never replaced. regular_performance_check(): 'diff = (opt_perf - perf)/opt_perf; if (diff > relative_tolerance) ... re-scan' (543-573).
failure_scenario: tune mode 'average' or 'median' with a noisy first sample of the first combination (e.g. a step right after setup): opt_perf is the outlier, every later check reports the performance as degraded, and the tuner keeps re-scanning instead of settling.
suggested_fix: Initialize opt_perf to the representative value of combination 0 (compute p_0 first) or to -1.0 so the loop always assigns it.

summary: unpack_3d_permute1_n_functor multiplies the fast-index plane stride by nqty ('nqty*fast*nstride_plane'), but the CPU reference src/pack.h advances the destination index by exactly nstride_plane per fast index, so for nqty > 2 the unpack scatters data to wrong (and out-of-range) locations.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h:302-305: 'const int instart = plane + nqty*mid; int in = instart + nqty*fast*nstride_plane; int out = out_orig + nqty*mid*nfast + nqty*fast; for (int iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) d_data[data_offset + in++] = d_buf[buf_offset + out++];'. src/pack.h:175-179 (unpack_3d_permute1_n): 'instart = plane + nqty * mid; for (fast = 0; fast < nfast; fast++, instart += nstride_plane) { in = instart; for (iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) data[in++] = buf[out++]; }' -- i.e. the destination index is plane + nqty*mid + fast*nstride_plane, with NO nqty factor on the stride (nstride_plane is already in units of scalars, remap_kokkos.cpp:524 sets 'nstride_plane = nqty*out.ksize*out.jsize'). The nqty==2 sibling in the same file confirms the correct form: pack_kokkos.h:245 'const int in = in_orig + fast*nstride_plane;' (no factor 2). The buf index 'out' is computed correctly.
failure_scenario: A remap plan created with permute==1 and nqty>=3 (remap_kokkos.cpp:436-437 selects unpack_3d_permute1_n) writes each fast plane nqty times too far apart: with nqty=3 the last plane lands at 3*(nfast-1)*nstride_plane, roughly three times past the end of the receive brick -> silently corrupted FFT/remap output or an out-of-bounds device write. Currently latent: every in-tree caller uses nqty=1 (pppm_kokkos.cpp:891) or nqty=2 (fft3d_kokkos.cpp:473,498,539,567), so the _n variants are never selected today.
suggested_fix: Drop the nqty factor: 'int in = instart + fast*nstride_plane;' (and the same in unpack_3d_permute2_n_functor).

summary: unpack_3d_permute2_n_functor has the same defect as the permute1_n variant: it multiplies the fast-index line stride by nqty ('nqty*fast*nstride_line') where src/pack.h advances by nstride_line only.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h:466-469: 'const int instart = nqty*slow + mid*nstride_plane; int in = instart + nqty*fast*nstride_line; int out = out_orig + nqty*mid*nfast + nqty*fast;'. src/pack.h:257-261 (unpack_3d_permute2_n): 'instart = nqty * slow + mid * nstride_plane; for (fast = 0; fast < nfast; fast++, instart += nstride_line) { in = instart; for (iqty = 0; iqty < nqty; iqty++) data[in++] = buf[out++]; }' -- destination index is nqty*slow + mid*nstride_plane + fast*nstride_line. The nqty==2 sibling pack_kokkos.h:411 'const int in = in_orig + fast*nstride_line;' has no factor 2, confirming the intended form.
failure_scenario: Same as the permute1_n case: a remap with permute==2 and nqty>=3 (remap_kokkos.cpp:444-445) scatters the unpacked values nqty times too far apart, corrupting the output brick or writing out of bounds. Latent today because no in-tree caller uses nqty>2.

summary: All eight pack/unpack functors decompose the flat Kokkos index so that the SLOW index varies fastest across threads, giving fully uncoalesced device loads and stores in every FFT remap.
evidence: pack_kokkos.h:73-76 (and identically at 128-131, 184-187, 238-241, 296-299, 351-354, 405-408, 461-464): 'const int fast = index / (nslow * nmid); const int index_new = index - (fast * nslow * nmid); const int mid = index_new / nslow; const int slow = index_new % nslow;'. Consecutive Kokkos indices therefore differ in 'slow', and the addresses used are 'd_buf[in_orig + mid*nfast + fast]' with in_orig = slow*nmid*nfast and 'd_data[plane + mid*nstride_line + fast]' with plane = slow*nstride_plane (line 77-82): adjacent threads are nmid*nfast resp. nstride_plane elements apart. The contiguous direction is 'fast' (src/pack.h:71 'for (fast = 0; ...) buf[in++] = data[out++]'), which here is the SLOWEST-varying thread index.
failure_scenario: No wrong results. On a GPU backend every remap in every 3d FFT (4 remaps per FFT, several FFTs per PPPM step) runs at a fraction of the achievable bandwidth because neither the read nor the write is coalesced.
suggested_fix: Swap the decomposition so 'fast' is the fastest-varying index (slow = index/(nmid*nfast); mid = (index/nfast)%nmid; fast = index%nfast), or use an MDRangePolicy with the fast index innermost.

summary: pack_kokkos.h has no include guard and includes the guard-less src/pack.h purely for 'struct pack_plan_3d', dragging ten unused static host functions into every translation unit that includes it.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pack_kokkos.h has no '#ifndef LMP_PACK_KOKKOS_H'; line 18 '#include "pack.h"'. src/pack.h likewise has no include guard and, under the default FFT_PACK_ARRAY (pack.h:25-27), defines pack_3d, unpack_3d and the six unpack_3d_permute* functions as file-static (pack.h:55-264). Including either header twice in one translation unit is a redefinition error; today only src/KOKKOS/remap_kokkos.cpp includes pack_kokkos.h, so this is latent.
failure_scenario: A future file including pack_kokkos.h together with pack.h (or including pack_kokkos.h twice through another header) fails to compile; meanwhile every build emits unused-static-function warnings for the ten CPU pack routines.
suggested_fix: Add '#ifndef LMP_PACK_KOKKOS_H' guards to both headers, and move 'struct pack_plan_3d' into its own small header (or forward-declare it) so pack_kokkos.h does not pull in the CPU implementations.

summary: With bzeroflag=1, chemflag=1 and wselfallflag=0 the KOKKOS evaluate_bi() subtracts bzero[j] from EVERY diagonal element triple (elem1==elem2==elem3), whereas the CPU SNA::compute_bi() subtracts it only from the one triple built from the central atom's element ielem, so pair snap/kk reports different energies than pair snap.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:1115-1125: 'register_loop<yi_batch>([&] (int n) -> void { bval[n] *= static_cast<accum_type>(2.0); if (bzero_flag) { if (!wselfall_flag) { if (elem1 == elem2 && elem1 == elem3) { bval[n] -= static_cast<accum_type>(bzero[j]); } } else { bval[n] -= static_cast<accum_type>(bzero[j]); } } });' -- evaluate_bi() never receives the central atom's element (its signature at sna_kokkos.h:340 and the caller compute_bi(iatom,jjb) at sna_kokkos_impl.h:1009 carry no ielem). src/ML-SNAP/sna.cpp:696-702: 'if (bzero_flag) { if (!wselfall_flag) { itriple = (ielem*nelements+ielem)*nelements+ielem; for (int jjb = 0; jjb < idxb_max; jjb++) { const int j = idxb[jjb].j; blist[itriple*idxb_max+jjb] -= bzero[j]; } } else { ... every triple ... } }' with ielem = the central atom's element (src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:346 'snaptr->compute_bi(ielem);'). For nelements > 1 the KOKKOS code shifts nelements diagonal triples instead of one. No compensating correction exists elsewhere: 'grep -n bzero src/KOKKOS/*' only matches sna_kokkos{.h,_impl.h}. blist feeds the energy directly (pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:1418 'evdwl += static_cast<accum_type>(d_coeffi[icoeff+1]*snaKK.blist(ii,idx_chem,idxb));').
failure_scenario: A multi-element SNAP potential with 'chemflag 1 bzeroflag 1 wselfallflag 0' (all legal; only wselfallflag differs from the shipped potentials/InP_JCPA2020.snapparam, which uses wselfallflag 1 and therefore hides the bug): every atom's energy is off by the constant -sum_{e != ielem} sum_jjb coeff_ielem[(e,e,e)*idxb_max+jjb+1]*bzero[j], so pair snap/kk and pair snap report different potential energies for the same configuration. Because the offset is position-independent, forces and stresses are unaffected, which is why force-based regression tests do not catch it.
suggested_fix: Pass the central atom's element into compute_bi()/evaluate_bi() (it is already available to the caller as d_map(type(i))) and gate the !wselfall_flag subtraction on 'elem1 == elem2 && elem2 == elem3 && elem1 == ielem', matching sna.cpp:698.

summary: SNAKokkos::compute_dsfac(), a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION, calls unqualified sin()/cos() instead of Kokkos::sin/Kokkos::cos, violating the KOKKOS device-math rule and silently promoting single-precision arguments to double; the function is also dead code.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:2265 'dsfac_outer = -onehalf * sin((r - rmin0) * rcutfac) * rcutfac;', :2283 'sfac_outer = onehalf * (cos((r - rmin0) * rcutfac) + one);', :2290 'sfac_inner = onehalf * (one - cos(static_cast<real_type>(MY_PI2) + (r - sinner) * rcutfac));', :2291 'dsfac_inner = onehalf * rcutfac * sin(...);'. The sibling routines do it correctly: compute_sfac uses 'Kokkos::cos' (:2231) and compute_s_dsfac uses 'Kokkos::sin'/'Kokkos::cos' (:2316-2317, :2328-2329). .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels ... never std::'. Grepping the package shows compute_dsfac is never called (only compute_sfac at :846 and compute_s_dsfac at :374 and :1832 are used).
failure_scenario: No current runtime effect because the function is unreachable; if it is ever wired back in, a SYCL/HIP build may fail to resolve the unqualified name and a real_type=float build loses precision through double promotion.
suggested_fix: Either delete compute_dsfac (and its declaration at sna_kokkos.h:372) since compute_s_dsfac supersedes it, or qualify the four calls with Kokkos::.

summary: sna_kokkos.h declares three member functions and one data member that have no definition and no caller anywhere in the tree.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos.h:482-486 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void create_team_scratch_arrays(const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team); ... void create_thread_scratch_arrays(const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team);' and :246-247 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION SNAKokkos(const SNAKokkos<DeviceType, real_type, accum_type, vector_length>& sna, const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team);' -- none of the three is defined in sna_kokkos_impl.h nor referenced anywhere ('grep -rn create_team_scratch_arrays src/' matches only this declaration). :409 'int twojmax, diagonalstyle;' -- diagonalstyle is never assigned or read (it is a leftover from the removed 'diagonal' SNAP option).
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; dead declarations mislead readers into thinking there is a team-scratch constructor path, and the uninitialized diagonalstyle member is a false lead when debugging.
suggested_fix: Delete the three declarations and the diagonalstyle member.

summary: memory_usage() selects the GPU vs CPU array set with 'if constexpr (!host_flag)' while grow_rij() allocates them under '!host_flag && !legacy_on_gpu', so with legacy_on_gpu enabled the reported memory omits the two largest arrays and counts five 1x1x1 dummies instead.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:323-339 'if (!host_flag && !legacy_on_gpu) { ...realloc a_gpu/b_gpu/da_gpu/db_gpu/sfac_gpu at full size...; realloc ulist_cpu/dulist_cpu at 1,1,1; } else { ...a_gpu etc at 1,1(,1)...; realloc ulist_cpu/dulist_cpu at natom_pad, nmax, idxu_cache_max; }' versus :2360-2369 'if constexpr (!host_flag) { bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(a_gpu); ... } else { bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(ulist_cpu); bytes += MemKK::memory_usage(dulist_cpu); }'. legacy_on_gpu is a runtime member (sna_kokkos.h:474) initialised from the owner (pair_snap_kokkos.h:87 'static constexpr bool legacy_on_gpu = false;'), so the two conditions only agree while that knob stays false.
failure_scenario: Flip pair_snap_kokkos.h's legacy_on_gpu to true (its documented purpose: 'run the CPU path on the GPU') and 'info memory'/the pair style's memory_usage() under-reports by natom_pad*nmax*idxu_cache_max*sizeof(complex)*4, the dominant allocation. No wrong physics.
suggested_fix: Use the same predicate in memory_usage(): 'if constexpr (!host_flag) if (!legacy_on_gpu) {gpu arrays} else {cpu arrays}', or factor the predicate into a single helper used by both.

summary: sna_kokkos_impl.h redefines MY_PI and MY_PI2 as file-static doubles directly in namespace LAMMPS_NS instead of using MathConst, giving every translation unit its own copy and setting up an ambiguity with MathConst::MY_PI.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h:29-30 'static const double MY_PI  = 3.14159265358979323846; // pi' and 'static const double MY_PI2  = 1.57079632679489661923; // pi/2', inside 'namespace LAMMPS_NS {' (line 27). src/math_const.h already provides LAMMPS_NS::MathConst::MY_PI and MY_PI2 with the same values; the CPU counterpart src/ML-SNAP/sna.cpp:23,31 does '#include "math_const.h"' + 'using namespace MathConst;'. Because this header is pulled into pair_snap_kokkos.cpp, compute_sna_grid_kokkos.cpp and compute_sna_grid_local_kokkos.cpp, any of those adding 'using namespace MathConst;' would make an unqualified MY_PI ambiguous.
failure_scenario: No current runtime effect. A later edit that adds 'using namespace MathConst;' to any TU including sna_kokkos.h fails to compile with an ambiguous-name error that points at an unrelated line.
suggested_fix: Delete the two definitions and use MathConst::MY_PI / MathConst::MY_PI2 (already available via math_const.h).
